gaps.concept: Primary hypothyroidism causes high TSH and low free T4; central hypothyroidism causes low free T4 with low or inappropriately normal TSH.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes thyroid failure from pituitary or hypothalamic disease in a hormone panel.

gaps.concept: Subclinical hypothyroidism has elevated TSH with normal free T4.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies early thyroid failure in an asymptomatic patient with an abnormal screening result.

gaps.concept: Hashimoto thyroid destruction is primarily T-cell mediated; thyroid antibodies are diagnostic markers.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the mechanism behind a painless goiter with positive anti-TPO antibodies.

gaps.concept: Primary hypothyroidism raises TRH, which can increase prolactin and cause galactorrhea or menstrual disturbance.
gaps.why_tested: Explains reproductive symptoms alongside high TSH and low free T4.

gaps.concept: Hypothyroid myxedema is nonpitting edema caused by dermal glycosaminoglycan accumulation.
gaps.why_tested: Asks for the tissue change underlying a puffy face or thickened skin.

gaps.concept: Severe hypothyroidism can cause pericardial effusion.
gaps.why_tested: Connects an enlarged cardiac silhouette with longstanding hypothyroid findings.

gaps.concept: Iodine deficiency causes low thyroid hormone, compensatory TSH elevation, and goiter; it is the leading worldwide cause of hypothyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cause of goiter and hypothyroidism in a patient from an iodine-deficient region.

gaps.concept: Lithium inhibits thyroid hormone release; excess iodine, including from amiodarone, can cause hypothyroidism through a persistent Wolff–Chaikoff effect.
gaps.why_tested: Explains new hypothyroidism after starting a characteristic medication.

gaps.concept: Thyroidectomy or radioactive iodine treatment can cause acquired hypothyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: Links a history of thyroid treatment to a later low free T4 and high TSH.

gaps.concept: De Quervain thyroiditis follows a viral illness and causes a painful thyroid, high ESR, granulomatous inflammation, and low radioactive iodine uptake.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes transient destructive thyroiditis from a hyperfunctioning thyroid disorder.

gaps.concept: Painless postpartum thyroiditis may cause transient thyrotoxicosis followed by hypothyroidism and has low radioactive iodine uptake.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cause of changing thyroid symptoms after delivery.

gaps.concept: Congenital hypothyroidism can result from failed thyroid descent, producing ectopic lingual thyroid tissue.
gaps.why_tested: Explains a newborn’s hypothyroidism with thyroid tissue at the tongue base.

gaps.concept: Inherited thyroid dyshormonogenesis, often involving thyroid peroxidase, causes congenital hypothyroidism despite a normally located gland.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a hormone-synthesis defect from thyroid dysgenesis in an affected newborn.

gaps.concept: In pregnancy, estrogen raises thyroid-binding globulin and total T4; free T4 stays near normal, while hCG can lower first-trimester TSH.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets thyroid tests in an otherwise euthyroid pregnant patient.

gaps.concept: Pregnancy increases levothyroxine requirements; adequate maternal T4 is essential for early fetal brain development.
gaps.why_tested: Explains rising TSH during pregnancy in a patient previously stable on levothyroxine.

gaps.concept: Levothyroxine is T4, a long-lived prohormone converted peripherally to active T3; TSH response to a dose change takes weeks.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the pharmacology behind delayed laboratory response to replacement therapy.

gaps.concept: Suspicious thyroid ultrasound features include a solid hypoechoic nodule, irregular margins, microcalcifications, and a taller-than-wide shape.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies which nodule warrants aspiration despite a normal TSH.

gaps.concept: A hard fixed thyroid nodule, cervical lymphadenopathy, or unexplained hoarseness raises concern for malignancy.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a concerning thyroid mass from a benign-appearing nodule on examination.

gaps.concept: Papillary thyroid carcinoma often has branching papillae with fibrovascular cores and can be multifocal or bilateral.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes additional histologic or gross findings in a papillary cancer specimen.

gaps.concept: Parafollicular C cells derive from neural crest cells via the ultimobranchial body.
gaps.why_tested: Asks the embryologic origin of medullary thyroid carcinoma.

gaps.concept: MEN2A pairs medullary carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and parathyroid hyperplasia; MEN2B pairs it with pheochromocytoma and mucosal neuromas.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes MEN2 subtypes from accompanying findings in a RET-associated cancer vignette.

gaps.concept: Medullary thyroid carcinoma can elevate CEA and cause secretory diarrhea; unlike follicular-cell cancers, it does not concentrate radioactive iodine.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the tumor from its markers, hormone effects, or lack of iodine uptake.

gaps.concept: Serum thyroglobulin can indicate persistent or recurrent differentiated thyroid cancer after thyroidectomy.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets a rising tumor marker after treatment of papillary or follicular carcinoma.

gaps.concept: Primary thyroid lymphoma is usually a B-cell lymphoma presenting as a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes lymphoma from another rapidly growing thyroid malignancy in a patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
